title: SSE/WSS scalability prober for chat completions with tokens/sec and p95 regression alerts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a scalable, production-like prober that can exercise our SSE and WebSocket streaming chat/completions endpoints at realistic concurrency (tens of thousands of open connections), measure tokens/sec and p95 token-emission latency, and automatically detect regressions vs baseline patterns.

Scope:
- Client drivers for both SSE and WSS that support: multiplexed connections, simulated network churn (disconnects/reconnects), backpressure, configurable prompt/sequence length distributions, and per-token emission timestamping.
- Orchestrator to schedule fleets of prober workers across k8s nodes or ephemeral cloud runners with controlled ramp profiles (constant, step, sawtooth, poisson arrivals).
- Metric collection pipeline: token-rate, token-emission p50/p95/p99, connection churn, reconnect latency, server-side error rates, KV-cache hit ratio, and per-model-variant breakdown. Metrics must be exported to Prometheus and sampled traces stored in S3 for offline analysis.
- Regression detection: baseline profiles stored per-commit and per-release; automated daily runs and on-PR smoke; anomaly detection triggers alerts when tokens/sec drops by >10% or p95 increases by >25% sustained over 5m. Alerts should create a ticket in Linear and post to #platform-perf.
- Replay support: capture real production conversation prefixes (sanitized) and replay to validate real-workload fidelity.
- Integrations: Grafana dashboard, Alertmanager rules, CI gate for runtime-1.22, and a GitHub action to run a scaled smoke on PRs.

Non-goals: Full A/B model scoring comparisons, e2e user-flows outside the chat/completions surface, client SDK changes to production clients.

Success metrics:
- Harness can sustain 40k concurrent persistent SSE connections or 25k WSS connections with a realistic token-emission distribution for 30m without worker OOMs.
- Produce stable tokens/sec measurement with <5% variance across 3 runs for the same profile.
- Regression pipeline detects injected performance regressions (benchmarked via synthetic slowdown) with <10 min time-to-alert.

Architecture notes:
- Worker binary in Go running evented SSE/WSS clients; uses tokio-like event loops; instrumented with per-token timestamps and backpressure counters.
- Coordinator service (Python/Flask) dispatches scenarios and collects worker heartbeats; stores run metadata in Postgres and traces in S3 (s3://redwood-loadtest-traces/ENG-87210/).
- Metrics emitted to Prometheus pushgateway when runs are ephemeral; long-term metrics recorded in Prometheus TSDB and ingested into the performance dashboard.
- Regression detection implemented as a nightly job that compares p95/tokens/sec to the baseline for the matching pipeline and model variant. Baseline generation also supports bootstrapping from last stable release (runtime-1.22).

Operational considerations:
- Account for cost: each full-scale run estimates ~120 GPU hours and we should provide a low-cost micro-run option for PRs.
- Safe replay: ensure PII scrubber for any captured prefixes.
- Run-time knobs: batch size, kv-cache priming ratio, sequence length mix, simulated token emission jitter.

Deliverables:
- driver binary + k8s helm chart for fleet runs
- coordinator + CLI to queue scenarios
- Prometheus/Grafana dashboards and Alertmanager rules
- CI/GitHub action smoke job and PR docs
- Runbook for interpreting regressions and triage steps

Links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE-WSS+Scalability+Prober ; sample dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming-prober/engine-perf ; baseline traces: s3://redwood-loadtest-traces/ENG-87210/baseline/
acceptance_criteria: Driver can open and maintain 40k concurrent SSE connections in a k8s cluster without worker OOMs
Driver emits per-token timestamps and metrics exported to Prometheus for tokens/sec and p95 latency
Automated nightly regression job compares runs to baseline and raises Linear ticket + Alertmanager alert when thresholds breached
Run artifacts (raw traces, metrics snapshot, run config) are archived to S3 with stable path format
Grafana dashboard panels for tokens/sec, p95/p99 emission latency, connection churn and KV-cache hit ratio are present and documented
comments: 2026-01-21 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting completed. Agreed on target scale (40k SSE / 25k WSS). Decided to implement driver in Go for lower memory overhead. Coordinator will be Python for faster iteration.
2026-01-26 - Mateo Ruiz: PoC driver can sustain 5k SSE connections on a single c5.4xlarge equivalent. Memory per connection ~1.4KB after optimizations. Pushing PR for event-loop and metric hooks.
2026-01-29 - Design review (Lara Kim): Dashboard layout approved; recommend adding per-model-variant split and a 'connectivity heatmap' for churn visualization. Added as AC #6.
2026-01-31 - Mateo Ruiz: PR opened - https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-load-tests/pull/412 - includes SSE/WSS client and basic orchestrator scaffolding.
2026-02-02 - Reliability feedback (Jonah Meyer): Add a safe-fail mode that downscales prober if token-rate impacts production metrics observed in same region. Marking as dependency: ENG-87991
